---
title: "Feature requests"
description: >-
  Ideas for what zotLook should do, and changes to what it does: where to put them, and what helps.
---

Have an idea for what zotLook should be able to do, or a change to suggest
to a feature or a setting it already has? Please open an issue on GitHub, as
you would for a bug:

**<https://github.com/fre-ms/zotLook/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml>**

I cannot promise it will be built, but I am glad of every idea: zotLook is a
plugin from the community for the community.

## What helps

- **What you want to achieve**, rather than the way to get there. The best
  way is often not the first one that comes to mind, and it is easier to
  find from the goal.
- **Which system** you are on. Much of what zotLook does is done differently
  on macOS, Linux and Windows, and a wish that is easy on one can be
  impossible on another.
- **Whether something already does it** — Zotero's own preview, or an
  [extension of the system's preview](platforms.qmd#extending-the-preview).
  zotLook builds on both deliberately, and a wish that one of them fulfils
  may be a matter of pointing at it.

## What zotLook is, and is not

A few things follow from how zotLook is built, and a request that runs with
them has a better chance than one that runs against them.

- **It drives the preview the system already has** and builds no viewer of
  its own. What the preview shows and how it behaves is the system's; what
  zotLook can change is what it hands over, and how.
- **A preview runs no scripts.** The contents and annotation menus, the page
  overview's links: all of it is markup and stylesheet, because a preview
  panel would ignore anything else. A wish that needs a script in the preview
  needs a different route.
- **One attachment at a time.** Selecting an item previews one of its
  attachments, chosen by a ranking you set; resolving them all would download
  every synced attachment of every selected item.
- **Annotations are read, not written.** zotLook shows the annotations Zotero
  keeps; editing them is the reader's job.

None of this is a closed door. It is where the plugin stands, so that a wish
can be placed in relation to it.
